opening.argument: The video is grounded in a specific eBay support dispute over an ordinary marketplace transaction: “This is a National Geographic Magazine. It sold for $7.50, plus they paid for shipping.” The speaker examines eBay’s handling of the matter, including a buyer’s feedback threat, listing-language criticism, tracking records, and the distinction between estimated and guaranteed delivery times. The shipment was not presented as a promised outcome; rather, the speaker reports that it “Showed up just as it stated on the second as a delay, which was stated as well.” The talking-head format and accompanying eBay order and tracking screens reinforce a reseller-advice or customer-complaint context. Finally, the audience requests are limited to routine distribution: “If you enjoyed the video, please hit that like button down below.” Nothing in these facts establishes a deceptive solicitation.
